description: Numbers transcribed from papers for the comets stage (coma brightness split, colours, dust dynamics, ion tail). Every entry names its source id (docs/sources/<id>.md; the PDF is kept with its sha256) and where in the paper the number is.

waterFromMagnitude.where: Results: log Q[H2O] = 30.675 (0.007) - 0.2453 (0.0013) mH; Q[H2O] = 1.1 Q[OH]; RMS of log Q residuals 0.190; 234 points, 37 comets, r = 0.32-4.53 au
waterFromMagnitude.note: mH is the visual magnitude reduced to Delta = 1 au (mV - 5 log Delta); with the SBDB total-magnitude law mH = M1 + K1 log10 r.

dustColour.where: Sect. 3 (Long Period Comets): mean colours of 26 LPCs B-V = 0.78+-0.02, V-R = 0.47+-0.02, R-I = 0.42+-0.03; (Active Short-Period Comets, from Solontoi et al. 2012) B-V = 0.80+-0.01, V-R = 0.46+-0.01; Table 3 last row: Sun B-V = 0.64+-0.02, V-R = 0.35+-0.01, R-I = 0.33+-0.01
dustColour.note: Broadband colours of active comae measured in apertures of a few arcsec, mostly of comets beyond ~2 au where gas emission contributes little: taken as the colour of the dust. Short-period comets have no R-I in the source; the long-period R-I excess is used for both.

oxygenRedDoublet.where: Table 4 footnote: branching ratio for O(1D) from H2O photodissociation 0.064, from OH photodissociation 0.357 (after Morgenthaler et al. 2001), OH yield of H2O photodissociation 0.81 (Huebner et al. 1992); Sect. 4 Eq. 1 text: beta6300 = 0.75, beta6364 = 0.25; Table 1: radiative rates A6300 = 6.44e-3 s-1, A6364 = 2.15e-3 s-1
oxygenRedDoublet.note: Photons per water molecule of the whole coma, collisional quenching of O(1D) in the inner coma neglected (an upper bound for very productive comets).

dustGrains.where: Moreno & Jehin (2025) Sect. 3: beta = C_pr Q_pr / (2 rho r), C_pr = 1.191e-3 kg m-2 (printed 1.191 x 10^3), Q_pr ~ 1 for r >~ 1 um (Mie, moderately absorbing grains); Agarwal et al. (2007) Eq. 9 beta = 3 L Q_pr / (16 pi c G M rho s), Table 1: 1P/Halley DIDSY > 20 um differential size index -3.5+-0.2, Stardust samples up to 1e-3 kg; Sect. 4: constant bulk density of 1000 kg/m3
dustGrains.note: beta is computed from the solar luminosity, GM_sun and c (Agarwal Eq. 9); Moreno & Jehin's C_pr is the same constant (checked by the stage). Grains below 1 um (Q_pr < 1, beta saturating) are left out.

dustEjection.where: Eq. 1: v(beta, rh, z) = v0 beta^gamma rh^Gamma (cos z)^eps, gamma <= 0.5 (Fulle 1987), Gamma = -0.5 (Whipple 1951; Reach et al. 2000); Eq. 2 and text: gamma = 0.25, v0 = 1 km/s (fitted for C/2023 A3)
dustEjection.note: Terminal speed of a grain relative to the nucleus; used for the widths of synchrones and syndynes (a grain shell of radius v tau around its zero-velocity position). Isotropic (the zenith-angle term averaged out).

haserVelocity.where: Table 3 caption: standard Haser model with v = 1 km s-1, g-factors from the Lowell Minor Planet Services and scale lengths as tabulated
haserVelocity.note: The Lowell Haser scale lengths are fitted with v = 1 km/s (A'Hearn et al. 1995), so the coma's total number of daughters is Q l_d / v with this v.

coPlus.where: Table 1: fluorescence efficiencies of 12CO+ (A2Pi - X2Sigma+, comet-tail system) at rh = 1 au, vh = 0, erg s-1 ion-1, rows v' = 0..5, columns v'' = 0..5; Table 4: wavelengths (A) of 12CO+ lines of the (3,0) and (2,0) bands
coPlus.note: Only the (3,0) and (2,0) bands have wavelengths in the source: the ion tail's spectrum is those two bands, each carrying its share of the total of Table 1 in proportion to its own efficiency (the other bands lie at 3800-5000 A too).

coAbundance.where: Sect. 2.2: Q_CO/Q_H2O from < 1% for C/2000 WM1 (LINEAR) to > 20% for C/1996 B2 (Hyakutake); CO/H2O varies by a factor of 50 across comets observed in the UV
coAbundance.note: The ion tail uses the geometric mean of the quoted range (4.5 %); an individual comet can be 5x brighter or fainter in CO+.
